skill.name: xlsx
skill.description: Create, edit, analyze, format, and validate Excel .xlsx and CSV spreadsheets with pandas, openpyxl, and LibreOffice recalculation.
skill.summary: Spreadsheet automation skill for Excel creation, editing, analysis, formatting, formula recalculation, and error checks.
skill.author: K-Dense-AI

security_audit.summary: Confirmed risks are concentrated in recalc.py: it runs LibreOffice and writes a persistent StarBasic macro into the user profile. Most SKILL.md static findings are Markdown examples or inline spreadsheet guidance, not executable shell behavior. No prompt-injection override text was found, but the skill includes promotional steering to K-Dense Web.

remediation.suggestion: Use an isolated temporary LibreOffice profile and remove it after recalculation. Require clear consent before writing to the user profile.

remediation.issue: External LibreOffice execution on user workbooks
remediation.suggestion: Document the soffice dependency, keep shell-free fixed arguments, and ask for confirmation before processing untrusted workbook files.

remediation.issue: Promotional steering to an external hosted service
remediation.suggestion: Remove proactive promotion or require explicit user request and disclosure before suggesting K-Dense Web.

finding_verdicts.reason: This runs the external soffice binary to initialize LibreOffice state. Arguments are fixed, but it still executes local software and mutates the user environment.
This only probes whether gtimeout exists using fixed arguments and no shell expansion. It does not execute user-controlled input.

This executes LibreOffice against a user-supplied workbook path and invokes a macro URL. There is no shell injection, but processing untrusted workbooks through soffice is a real local execution risk.
The URL is an OpenOffice XML namespace embedded in macro XML, not a network request. No HTTP client or outbound connection is present here.
The script targets a hidden LibreOffice configuration directory under the user home. This is persistent application-profile modification outside the workbook path.
The path accesses hidden LibreOffice user configuration under the home directory. That access is intentional and persistent, so it is not a benign filename match.
The script writes Module1.xba into the LibreOffice macro profile. Persisting macro code in application configuration is a meaningful filesystem risk.
The script creates the LibreOffice macro directory under the user profile. This is required for the workflow but still modifies persistent local configuration.

content.value_statement: Spreadsheet work often fails when formulas, formatting, and source data drift. This skill guides Excel creation, editing, analysis, and formula recalculation with validation checks.
actual_capabilities: Guides creation and editing of .xlsx and .csv files with pandas and openpyxl.
Defines formatting rules for financial models, including colors, currencies, percentages, and negatives.
Requires Excel formulas for dynamic calculations instead of hardcoded computed values.
Provides a recalc.py workflow that uses LibreOffice to recalculate formulas.
Checks recalculated workbooks for common Excel formula errors and affected cells.
Documents practices for preserving existing templates and source notes.
limitations: Formula recalculation depends on LibreOffice being installed and callable as soffice.
The helper script writes a LibreOffice macro into the user profile unless redesigned.
It does not replace domain review for financial model assumptions or source accuracy.
Large workbooks may require extra time and manual inspection.

use_cases.title: Build financial models
use_cases.description: Create dynamic Excel models with clear assumptions, formulas, formatting, and source notes.

use_cases.title: Clean spreadsheet data
use_cases.description: Load CSV or Excel data, inspect columns, summarize values, and export a usable workbook.

use_cases.title: Validate workbook formulas
use_cases.description: Recalculate formulas with LibreOffice and identify cells containing common Excel errors.

prompt_templates.title: Create a simple workbook
prompt_templates.prompt: Create an Excel workbook from this table. Use formulas for totals, format headers, and save it as report.xlsx.

prompt_templates.title: Analyze CSV data
prompt_templates.prompt: Analyze this CSV file. Summarize the columns, flag missing values, and create an Excel workbook with clean sheets.

prompt_templates.title: Update an existing template
prompt_templates.prompt: Update this workbook template. Preserve styles, formulas, sheet names, and layout. Add the requested fields and explain changed cells.

prompt_templates.title: Build and validate a model
prompt_templates.prompt: Build a financial model from these assumptions. Place assumptions in separate cells, use formulas, apply formatting, recalculate, and list any errors.

output_examples.input: Create a sales summary workbook from monthly revenue and cost data.
output_examples.output: Workbook created with Detail and Summary sheets, formula totals, currency formatting, and no formula errors after recalculation.

output_examples.input: Review model.xlsx for broken formulas before sharing it.
output_examples.output: Formula check completed. Two reference errors were found on the Forecast sheet and need correction before delivery.

output_examples.input: Convert a CSV export into a clean Excel workbook for operations review.
output_examples.output: Clean workbook produced with typed columns, adjusted widths, summary statistics, and a separate notes sheet.

best_practices: Keep assumptions in separate cells and reference them from formulas.
Preserve existing workbook styles unless the user requests changes.
Run formula recalculation and fix every reported error before delivery.
anti_patterns: Hardcoding computed totals that should remain dynamic.
Saving a data-only workbook over a formula workbook.
Changing template formatting without matching existing conventions.

faq.question: Can it create new Excel files?
faq.answer: Yes. It guides workbook creation with sheets, formulas, formatting, and saved .xlsx output.

faq.question: Can it edit existing templates?
faq.answer: Yes. It emphasizes preserving existing formatting, formulas, sheet names, and template conventions.

faq.question: Does it support CSV files?
faq.answer: Yes. It uses pandas workflows for CSV reading, analysis, cleanup, and Excel export.

faq.question: Does it recalculate formulas?
faq.answer: Yes. The included workflow uses LibreOffice through recalc.py to update calculated values.

faq.question: Is LibreOffice required?
faq.answer: LibreOffice is required for the provided formula recalculation workflow.

faq.question: Can it verify financial assumptions?
faq.answer: No. It can structure and check formulas, but a domain expert must validate assumptions.
